For ICP-MS, a lower calibration range was used in order to capture trace elements. A 0.5-50 ppb range was selected for this instrument. This range was determined by prior trial and error for other uranium-alloy samples. Preparations were made at 0 ppb, 0.5 ppb, 5 ppb, and a 50 ppb with a 20 ppb verification standard to check for accuracy, and an internal standard at 20 ppb added to each sample and standard to account for variability across each sample. Each calibration standard was created by adding 1 mL of internal standard (1 ppm Tm, Rh, and Sc) in each 50 mL falcon tube, along with designated amounts of equal parts of the custom calibration standards with 1% HNO3 . Three microscopy preparations were used to highlight different features. The first is an otherwise untreated high polish for imaging using an SEM in backscattered mode and utilizing EDS for semi-quantitative local chemistry interogation. This was especially important to determine the presence of initially solidified 27 molybdenum phase regions and to understand the ultimate amplitude of the microsegregation after solidification and cooling. The second is a preferential oxidation treatment outlined in detail by S. D. Imhoff et al. (2018).
